original_question: For the standard symplectic torus T^{2n} with n > 1, is the Hofer-Zehnder capacity finite?
target_in_paper: Section 2, parenthetical open problem immediately after Proposition 2.2: "It seems to be unknown whether or not T^{2n} with the standard symplectic structure has finite capacity for n > 1."
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended target very closely: it singles out the standard symplectic torus T^{2n}, uses the correct dimension restriction n > 1, and asks exactly about finiteness of the Hofer-Zehnder capacity rather than a broader periodic-orbit question. It also correctly avoids the irrational translation-invariant symplectic form discussed in Example 2.3.
missing_details: State the torus and symplectic form explicitly, e.g. T^{2n} = R^{2n}/Z^{2n} with the standard translation-invariant symplectic form ω_std = Σ_{j=1}^n dx_j∧dy_j.
Write the capacity in the paper's notation as c_HZ(T^{2n}, ω_std).
Make the quantifier explicit: for each n > 1 (equivalently 2n ≥ 4).

Clarify that "finite" means the Hofer-Zehnder capacity of the compact symplectic manifold itself is finite, i.e. c_HZ(T^{2n}, ω_std) < ∞, not merely an almost-existence statement for some class of Hamiltonians.

Keep the hypothesis "standard symplectic structure" explicit, because the paper immediately contrasts this with an irrational translation-invariant symplectic form ω_irr on T^{2n}, for which c_HZ(T^{2n}, ω_irr) = ∞ by Proposition 2.2 and Example 2.3.
refined_question: For each n > 1, let T^{2n} = R^{2n}/Z^{2n} be equipped with the standard translation-invariant symplectic form ω_std = Σ_{j=1}^n dx_j∧dy_j. Is the Hofer-Zehnder capacity of this compact symplectic torus finite; equivalently, is c_HZ(T^{2n}, ω_std) < ∞?
justification: The draft is aiming at a specific unlabeled open problem in Section 2, not at the paper's broader main question about the size of the aperiodic set AP_H. Right after Proposition 2.2, the paper explicitly says that it is unknown whether T^{2n} with the standard symplectic structure has finite capacity for n > 1. The nearby context defines c_HZ and the notion of bounded capacity, which explains exactly what "finite capacity" means here. Example 2.3 on the same page then shows that the analogous statement fails for an irrational translation-invariant symplectic form on T^{2n}, so specifying the standard symplectic structure is essential and should not be dropped.

citations.label: definition of c_HZ and bounded capacity immediately preceding Proposition 2.2
